checks.label: Now we can apply Ohm's Law, I = E/Z: on the series screen, at every resistance and reactance tested, the current arrow I is the supply's arrow V divided by Z's arrow, R + jX, as complex numbers

The phase angle between voltage and current is the same as the phase angle of the impedance: at every setting tested, the angle from I's arrow round to V's is Z's angle, and I's length times Z's is V's

Dragging Z up shrinks I and swings it further back, and below the real axis I swings ahead: with R = 8 Ω, for every whole ohm of X from −20 to 20 Ω, I's angle falls as X rises, from ahead of V to behind it, and I is longest, 28.75 A, at X = 0

Impedances add in series; reciprocals of impedances add in parallel: on the voltages screen I × R and I × jX end exactly on V's tip at every setting tested, and side by side the supply current is V times the sum of the branches' reciprocal impedances, the same as V divided by product over sum, which the product-over-sum screen draws

Just as with DC circuits, branch currents in a parallel AC circuit add to form the total current: on the side-by-side screen, at every setting tested, the supply's arrow I runs from 0 to the tip of I₂, laid at the tip of I₁; with the capacitor switched off the supply gives I₁ alone

Resistive impedance points right, inductive impedance with its 90° phase angle points up and capacitive impedance with its −90° phase angle points down: the capacitor branch's Z₂ is drawn straight down, its current I₂ stands straight up from the supply's 0° at every capacitor setting tested, and across a coil I × jX stands a quarter turn ahead of I × R, across a capacitor a quarter turn behind
The mains supply in the UK is 230 volts: V is drawn as 230∠0° V, the same arrow, on every screen but the meter puzzle, which asks for it, and in every answer

By adding the capacitor, the two reactive currents cancel: with the example coil, as the capacitor's current grows the supply current's j part shrinks to nearly nothing, where the supply current is least, and beyond that it grows again
To divide, we divide their moduli and subtract their arguments: the opening screen draws I first as the supply's length divided by Z's, along V, then turns it back by Z's argument

From outside the rule: the practice motor, 12 + j16 Ω on 230 V, is √400 = 20∠53.13° Ω and draws 11.5 A, 6.9 − j9.2 in parts; a capacitor of 230 ÷ 9.2 = 25 Ω cancels that j part, which at 50 Hz is 1 ÷ (2π × 50 × 25) = 127.3 µF

Each puzzle takes only its right answer: its three answers differ, the right one matches a working done separately here and only it is drawn without a mistake; each wrong one is drawn as what its slip makes, in red
Before an answer, a puzzle shows only its question: no working, nothing marked as a mistake and not its answer's arrow

Every demonstration finishes within 4.8 s of its screen opening and none starts before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 3 s; and a drag or slider move on a free screen shows its result at once

warnings: The page height keeps growing with the frame (avoid vh units and height:100%). [at 340 px wide]
SVG labels "10" and "Z" are touching on one row, so they read as one: leave at least 4 px between them, or label only what differs (at X = −j20 Ω, and 1 more setting)
SVG labels "I₁" and "I" are touching on one row, so they read as one: leave at least 4 px between them, or label only what differs (at XC = −j40 Ω, and 1 more setting) [at 340 px wide]
